text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl says he doubts the will of opposition Social Democrat (SPD) leader Oskar Lafontaine to reach agreement on planned tax reforms.
- Turks protest in Dortmund after fire last week in which Turkish woman and her two children died.
- Trial of disgraced tycoon Juergen Schneider charged with fraud likely to start on June 30.
- Germany's six leading economic research institutes -- in a semiannual report -- forecast 1997 growth of 2.25 percent and a public sector deficit of 3.0 to 3.2 percent of economic output this year.
- Two of phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG's main rivals file regulatory complaints with the government, accusing the former monopoly of preventing fair competition.
- M3 money supply growth slows to 8.3 percent in March.
- Kohl lays out conditions ahead of tax reform summit with Lafontaine planned for Wednesday.
- SPD's Lafontaine calls the promises Kohl's coalition over tax reform "unrealistic" and calculates that the plans will not provide relief.
- VfB Stuttgart's Brazilian striker Giovane Elber set to join Bayern Munich in the close season.
- SPD questions the financing of the ruling coalition's tax reform plans.
- Italian President Luigi Scalfaro meets German President Roman Herzog in Berlin on second day of visit to country.

- Leading economic research institutes forecast 1997 growth of just 2.25 percent and say Germany can be among first members of European monetary union (EMU) although the country's budget deficit could overshoot the 3.0 percent deficit to gross domestic product EMU target.
